prompt: AP-A is configured individually and handles its own WLAN policy. AP-B obtains that policy from a WLC. Which architecture comparison fits?
options: Both are autonomous because both perform radio acknowledgements
Both are cloud-managed because each has an IP address
explanation: An AP configured individually is autonomous; an AP that takes its WLAN policy from a WLC is controller-based.

whyWrong.2: Radio acknowledgements happen in every architecture, so they do not identify autonomous APs.
whyWrong.3: An IP address does not make an AP cloud-managed.

prompt: Which work remains in a Cisco lightweight AP in the split-MAC architecture?
options: Selecting all campus client VLAN mappings
explanation: In split-MAC the AP keeps real-time 802.11 work such as acknowledgements. The WLC handles authentication, roaming, RF management and VLAN mapping.

whyWrong.0: RADIUS policy is set on the controller and authentication server, not the AP.
whyWrong.1: VLAN mapping is a WLC function in split-MAC.
whyWrong.3: A lightweight AP downloads its configuration from the WLC and does not keep it.

prompt: Which controller UDP ports does CAPWAP use for control and data respectively?
explanation: CAPWAP control uses controller UDP port 5246 and data uses UDP port 5247.

exhibit.title: Representative AireOS interface summary
exhibit.text:
Interface    VLAN  IP Address       Type     Ap Mgr
management   10    192.168.10.5     Static   Yes
users        20    192.168.20.5     Dynamic  No
virtual      N/A   192.0.2.1        Static   No

prompt: Which interface is shown providing the AP-manager function on this AireOS controller?
options: The service port outside this table
explanation: The management interface has `Ap Mgr Yes`, so APs join through it. Dynamic interfaces map client VLANs and the virtual interface serves DHCP relay and web authentication.

whyWrong.0: The users interface is a dynamic client VLAN interface with Ap Mgr No.
whyWrong.1: The virtual interface is not where APs join.
whyWrong.2: The exhibit shows no service-port AP-manager function.

prompt: Which two AP modes dedicate the AP to observation instead of serving clients? (Choose two.)
explanation: A monitor-mode AP is a dedicated sensor, and a sniffer-mode AP captures frames on one channel for an analyzer PC. Neither serves ordinary clients.

whyWrong.4: Bridge mode can include client access.

prompt: Which two statements correctly separate CAPWAP protection from wireless-link protection? (Choose two.)
options: CAPWAP discovery occurs before the protected control session
WPA2 encrypts client payloads across every wired CAPWAP path
Established Cisco AP control traffic normally uses DTLS
Data and control always share one mandatory DTLS policy
A controller needs TCP 5247 for centrally switched data
explanation: CAPWAP discovery is unencrypted and happens before the DTLS-protected control session. CAPWAP data encryption is a separate, optional setting.

whyWrong.1: WPA2 protects only the radio link, not the wired CAPWAP tunnel.
whyWrong.3: Data encryption is a separate setting from control DTLS.
whyWrong.4: CAPWAP data uses UDP 5247, not TCP.

prompt: An AireOS model has a dedicated service port. What is its intended purpose?
options: Carry every client VLAN through an 802.1Q trunk
Negotiate a dynamic LACP bundle with every AP
Provide the virtual address used by a guest portal
explanation: The service port gives out-of-band management for setup and recovery, and connects to a switch access port.

whyWrong.0: Client VLANs use the distribution-system ports.
whyWrong.2: The service port does not aggregate AP links.
whyWrong.3: The virtual interface provides the guest-portal address.

prompt: A branch with eight APs has no separate controller hardware. One of the APs runs the controller function for the others. Which WLC deployment model is this?
explanation: Mobility Express runs the controller function inside one of the APs, which suits a small branch. It supports the fewest APs of the four models.

whyWrong.0: A unified deployment uses a dedicated controller appliance at a central site.
whyWrong.1: A cloud-based controller runs as a virtual machine in a data center or cloud.
whyWrong.2: An embedded controller runs inside an access-layer switch, not an AP.

prompt: An engineer suspects a cordless phone is interfering with a WLAN. Which AP mode dedicates the radios to spectrum analysis for a PC running analysis software?
explanation: SE-Connect dedicates the radios to spectrum analysis, which shows non-Wi-Fi interference. The AP serves no clients in this mode.

whyWrong.0: Sniffer mode captures 802.11 frames, and a cordless phone does not send them.
whyWrong.2: Monitor mode is a sensor for rogue devices, intrusion detection and location.
whyWrong.3: A rogue detector listens on the wired network with its radios off.

prompt: On an AireOS controller, WLAN STAFF must place its clients in wired VLAN 20. Which interface type provides that mapping?
explanation: A dynamic interface maps a WLAN to a wired VLAN, with an IP address, gateway and DHCP server in that VLAN.

whyWrong.1: The virtual interface supports DHCP relay and web authentication.
whyWrong.2: The management interface is for in-band management and AP joins.
whyWrong.3: The service-port interface is for out-of-band management.

prompt: AP1 sends management untagged in VLAN 10 and locally switched clients tagged in VLANs 20 and 30. Which port configuration matches?
options: Access VLAN 10 with all client traffic untagged
Access VLAN 20 with a voice VLAN of 30
explanation: Untagged management traffic uses the native VLAN, 10. VLANs 20 and 30 stay tagged, and the allowed list must include all three.

whyWrong.0: An access port cannot carry tagged client VLANs.
whyWrong.1: An access port with a voice VLAN does not match an AP that needs a trunk.
whyWrong.2: Native VLAN 20 puts management in the wrong VLAN and the list omits VLAN 10.

prompt: A centrally switched AP sends only untagged management traffic into VLAN 10. Which switchport configuration matches?
options: Access VLAN 10, carrying the AP's outer traffic
Access VLAN 20, matching the users' subnet
Trunk native VLAN 20 with VLAN 10 excluded
Routed port addressed from the client subnet
explanation: An access port in VLAN 10 carries the AP's untagged CAPWAP traffic. With central switching, client VLANs appear at the controller, not the AP.

whyWrong.1: The AP's own traffic is in VLAN 10, not the clients' VLAN.
whyWrong.2: Native VLAN 20 with VLAN 10 excluded does not carry the AP's management network.
whyWrong.3: An AP needs a Layer 2 attachment to VLAN 10, not a routed port.

prompt: A Meraki SSID is in bridge mode. A client prints to a server in the same local client VLAN. Where does the traffic go?
options: Through the AP and the cloud manager before entering the printer VLAN
Through a CAPWAP tunnel to a central WLC before entering the printer VLAN
Through the AP directly into the local wired printer VLAN
Through the branch router to an Internet gateway and back to the local VLAN
explanation: In bridge mode the AP forwards client traffic straight into the local wired VLAN. The cloud dashboard manages the AP but is not in the data path.

whyWrong.0: The cloud manager is a management plane, not a data-path hop.
whyWrong.1: A bridge-mode SSID does not tunnel to a WLC.
whyWrong.3: Same-VLAN traffic needs no routed Internet detour.

exhibit.title: Power worksheet — representative, model requirements supplied
exhibit.text:
AP model guide: full radio operation requires 802.3at power
Switch: AP powered, 802.3af allocation only
Controller: AP joined; radio capability restricted by low power

prompt: A powered AP runs with reduced radio capability. What is the next check?
options: Add a second uplink before checking whether the AP supports aggregation
Keep the present allocation because the AP has already registered
Move management to a tagged VLAN before checking the power source
Compare required PoE with negotiated allocation and remaining switch budget
explanation: The controller reports a low-power restriction, so compare the AP's PoE requirement with what the port negotiated and the switch's remaining budget.

whyWrong.0: A second uplink does not replace adequate PoE power.
whyWrong.1: Registering does not prove the AP has full power.
whyWrong.2: Tagging the management VLAN does not fix a power shortfall.

prompt: AP1 centrally switches a WLAN into VLAN 40 at WLC1. AP management is untagged in VLAN 10 on an access port. Where must VLAN 40 be carried?
options: On the AP access link, replacing its management VLAN
On the controller's separate out-of-band service port
On the WLC's distribution trunk toward the VLAN 40 service path
On every routed link between AP1 and WLC1
explanation: With central switching, the client VLAN emerges at the WLC, so VLAN 40 is carried on the WLC's distribution trunk. The AP link carries only its CAPWAP management traffic.

whyWrong.0: Client traffic is inside the CAPWAP tunnel, so the AP port stays in VLAN 10.
whyWrong.1: The service port is for out-of-band management only.
whyWrong.3: Routed CAPWAP transport does not need the client VLAN on each hop.

prompt: A FlexConnect WLAN switches clients locally and keeps local DHCP and gateway services during a WAN failure. New Enterprise authentication needs RADIUS across the failed WAN. What happens?
options: Both existing forwarding and new Enterprise authentication must stop together
Existing local forwarding may continue while new Enterprise authentication fails
New Enterprise authentication succeeds because local switching replaces RADIUS
All clients move to central switching while the WAN remains unavailable
explanation: Local switching keeps forwarding for connected clients. A new 802.1X client needs the unreachable RADIUS server, so it cannot authenticate.

whyWrong.0: Forwarding is local and does not depend on the WAN.
whyWrong.2: Local switching does not replace RADIUS authentication.
whyWrong.3: A failed WAN cannot carry centrally switched traffic.

prompt: AP1 sends management untagged and staff frames tagged VLAN 20. Its management VLAN is 10. SW1's AP trunk allows 10,20 with native VLAN 20. What is the fix?
options: Change the native VLAN to 10 and preserve allowed VLANs 10,20
Remove VLAN 10 and make staff traffic untagged
Change the AP-facing port to access VLAN 20
Change the native VLAN to 10 and allow only VLAN 10
explanation: Untagged management frames must enter VLAN 10, so set the native VLAN to 10. Keep VLAN 20 allowed for the tagged staff traffic.

whyWrong.1: Removing VLAN 10 drops the management network.
whyWrong.2: An access port cannot carry the tagged staff VLAN.
whyWrong.3: Allowing only VLAN 10 breaks staff traffic.

prompt: A controller lists AP1 as operational with a management address, but no client has been tested. What proves client service works?
options: Fresh client security, intended IP settings and successful service test
A saved controller configuration and unchanged AP count
A second management ping to the same AP address
A DHCP binding naming the AP's wired MAC address
explanation: A registered AP proves only the infrastructure path. A client that authenticates, gets the intended IP settings and reaches a service proves the client path.

whyWrong.1: A saved configuration and AP count show neither client authentication nor addressing.
whyWrong.2: A second management ping repeats management-plane evidence.
whyWrong.3: The AP's own lease is not a wireless client's lease.

prompt: The AP guide supports a two-port LACP bundle with the AP negotiating passively. Which switch mode initiates the bundle?
options: LACP passive on both switch members
PAgP desirable on both switch members
LACP active on both switch members
Static mode on with negotiation disabled
explanation: At least one LACP end must be active. The AP is passive, so the switch must be active.

whyWrong.0: Passive on both ends never starts LACP.

prompt: SW1 ports Gi1/0/1 and Gi1/0/2 connect to the distribution ports of an AireOS controller with LAG enabled. Both switch ports are matching 802.1Q trunks. Which command completes the bundle on SW1?
explanation: An AireOS LAG is static and runs neither LACP nor PAgP, so the switch side uses `channel-group` mode `on`.

whyWrong.0: Active starts LACP, which AireOS does not run.
whyWrong.1: Desirable starts PAgP, which AireOS does not run.
whyWrong.3: Passive waits for LACP packets that the controller never sends.

exhibit.title: Controlled diagnostic record — representative
exhibit.text:
AP management lease/gateway: valid
AP has no remembered or configured WLC address
DHCP option 43: absent; controller DNS lookup: no record
Router does not relay local CAPWAP discovery broadcasts
Authorized probe to WLC UDP 5246: controller responds
AP capture: local discovery only; no remote WLC destination

prompt: A new, unprimed AP is on a different subnet from its WLC. Which missing item does this record show?
options: A change from central switching to local switching
A lease pool for the wireless staff clients
A trunk carrying the remote client VLAN to the AP
A method for discovering a controller address
explanation: The AP has IP connectivity but no controller candidate: broadcast does not cross the router, and no stored address, option 43 or DNS record exists. Configure a discovery method.

whyWrong.0: Switching mode does not affect controller discovery.
whyWrong.1: The failure is AP discovery, before any client service matters.
whyWrong.2: Central switching does not need the client VLAN at the AP.

prompt: Which DNS name does a Cisco AP look up to find a controller?
explanation: A Cisco AP resolves CISCO-CAPWAP-CONTROLLER in the domain its DHCP lease supplied. This is one of four discovery sources.

whyWrong.1: Cisco APs do not look up this name.
whyWrong.2: Cisco APs do not look up this name.
whyWrong.3: Cisco APs do not look up this name.

prompt: What is the default protection for CAPWAP data traffic on UDP 5247?
explanation: CAPWAP data is unencrypted by default and DTLS is an optional setting. Only control traffic is always DTLS-encrypted.

whyWrong.1: DTLS on data is optional, not always on.
whyWrong.2: WPA2 protects the radio link, not the CAPWAP tunnel.

prompt: Which function moves from the AP to the WLC in Cisco's split-MAC design?
explanation: In split-MAC, authentication, roaming, RF management and VLAN mapping move to the WLC. Real-time 802.11 work stays in the AP.

whyWrong.0: Acknowledgements are real-time work that stays in the AP.
whyWrong.1: Beacon transmission is real-time work that stays in the AP.
whyWrong.3: Signal encoding is real-time radio work that stays in the AP.

prompt: Which setting is the default on Cisco PoE ports, letting the port detect and power an AP?
explanation: `power inline auto` is the default on Cisco PoE ports and lets the port detect and power the device.

whyWrong.0: `never` disables PoE and is not the default.
whyWrong.2: `static` pre-allocates power and is not the default.
whyWrong.3: `consumption` sets a power value and is not the default.
